questions.q: If f : R → R is f(x) = x⁴, then —
options: f is one-one but not onto
f is neither one-one nor onto
questions.work: f(−1) = f(1) = 1, so not one-one. No real x gives f(x) = −1, so not onto.

sections.title: Objective type questions of two 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) If f(x) = (x − 1)/|x − 1|, x ≠ 1, the range of f is ______. (b) If f(x) = 2x³ − 1, then f⁻¹(x) = ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) If a * b = b − 2a, then (1 * 2) * 3 = ______. (b) R is ______ if (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R.
True or False: (a) 'is a factor of' on R is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. (b) f(x) = x² + 3 on R is one-one and onto.
questions.answer:
(a) True — a | a; a | b, b | c ⇒ a | c; but 2 | 4 while 4 ∤ 2.
(b) False — f(−1) = f(1), and values below 3 are not attained.

sections.title: Objective type questions of four 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Answer: (a) Is R = {(1,2), (2,1)} on {1, 2, 3} an equivalence relation? (b) Is f(x) = 3 − 4x on R one-one and onto? (c) If f(x) = 2ˣ, find (f∘f)(0). (d) A binary operation on A is a function from ______ to A.
questions.answer:
(a) No — (1,1) ∉ R, so it is not reflexive (it is also not transitive: (1,2), (2,1) but no (1,1)).
(b) Yes. One-one: 3 − 4a = 3 − 4b ⇒ a = b. Onto: for any y, x = (3 − y)/4 gives f(x) = y.
(c) f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2 ⇒ (f∘f)(0) = 2.
(d) A × A.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and R = {(2, 3)}, check whether R is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.
questions.answer:
Not reflexive: (1,1) ∉ R.
Not symmetric: (2,3) ∈ R but (3,2) ∉ R.
Transitive: there are no pairs (a,b), (b,c) both in R, so the condition holds vacuously.

questions.q: Show that the signum function f(x) = 1 (x > 0), 0 (x = 0), −1 (x < 0) on R is neither one-one nor onto.
questions.answer:
f(1) = f(2) = 1, so it is not one-one.
Its range is {−1, 0, 1}; for example 2 has no pre-image, so it is not onto.

questions.q: Show that the relation 'T₁ is similar to T₂' on the set of all triangles is an equivalence relation.
questions.answer:
Reflexive: every triangle is similar to itself.
Symmetric: if T₁ ~ T₂ (corresponding angles equal), then T₂ ~ T₁.
Transitive: if T₁ ~ T₂ and T₂ ~ T₃, the angles of T₁ equal those of T₃, so T₁ ~ T₃.
Hence R is an equivalence relation.

questions.q: Show that (a, b) R (c, d) ⇔ ad = bc is an equivalence relation on N × N.
questions.answer:
Reflexive: ab = ba ⇒ (a, b) R (a, b).
Symmetric: ad = bc ⇒ cb = da ⇒ (c, d) R (a, b).
Transitive: ad = bc and cf = de. Multiply: adcf = bcde ⇒ af = be (c, d ≠ 0) ⇒ (a, b) R (e, f).
Hence R is an equivalence relation.

questions.q: Let f : R⁺ → (−4, ∞), f(x) = x² − 4. Show that f is invertible and find f⁻¹.
questions.answer:
One-one: x₁² − 4 = x₂² − 4 ⇒ x₁ = x₂ (both positive).
Onto: for y > −4, x = √(y + 4) > 0 and f(x) = y.
So f is invertible and f⁻¹(y) = √(y + 4).

questions.q: Show that f : R → R, f(x) = x² − 1 is neither one-one nor onto.
questions.answer:
f(1) = f(−1) = 0, so it is not one-one.
x² − 1 ≥ −1 for all x, so −2 has no pre-image: not onto.
